newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-BRAVES TURN TO MADDUX FOR GAME SIX AGAINST CARDINALS.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-BRAVES TURN TO MADDUX FOR GAME SIX AGAINST CARDINALS.

text.p: The Atlanta Braves, who stayed alive with a record-setting 14-0 rout of the Cardinals in St Louis Monday, turn to four-time Cy Young winner Greg Maddux for the sixth game of the NL Championship Series Wednesday.
The Cardinals won three straight after dropping the opener in the best-of-seven National League series and had a chance to finish off Atlanta at home Monday.
But with their backs against the wall, the Braves came out swinging and demolished the Cards to pull within three games to two with the series shifting back to Atlanta.
The defending World Series champions collected 22 hits, smashing the NLCS mark of 16 set by the Chicago Cubs in 1984 and the ALCS record of 19 set by the New York Yankees in 1981.
The winner of the National League series will face the Yankees in the World Series, beginning Saturday in New York.
Maddux dominated the Cardinals during the regular season, going 2-0 with a 0.78 ERA in three starts against them.

But he was roughed up for eight runs -- three earned -- and nine hits over 6 2/3 innings in an 8-3 loss to the Cardinals in Game Two of the NLCS last Thursday. Gary Gaetti's grand slam in the seventh inning was the knockout punch.
St Louis counters Wednesday with Donovan Osborne. The lefty allowed two runs on seven hits over seven innings in a 3-2 win over Atlanta in the third game of the series Saturday.
Atlanta is hoping to become the first team to rally from a 3-1 deficit to win the National League Championship Series.

Javy Lopez and Mark Lemke each had four hits for the Braves, and John Smoltz broke the post-season strikeout mark as he breezed to his 27th win of the season, including three in the playoffs, for the Braves Monday.
The National League Cy Young Award favourite threw seven innings, allowing seven hits and a walk while striking out seven as he improved his post-season career mark to 8-1.
The Yankees will make their record 34th trip to the World Series after closing out the Baltimore Orioles 6-4 Sunday to win the ALCS by four games to one.
The Yankees will be making their first trip to the World Series since losing to the Los Angeles Dodgers in six games in 1981 classic.
The individual who waited the longest for a trip to baseball's showcase is Yankees manager Joe Torre.
Torre, who starred as a player for both the Cardinals and Braves and also later managed both teams, has participated in 4,272 games as a player and manager and will be part of his first World Series.
